alerts.title: Weight gain likely from undertreated hypothyroidism, not DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines note the association between DTG and weight gain appears non-causal, instead reflecting less metabolic toxicity than older regimens. Patient gained 9 kg over one year with BMI 33, but has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target <4.5), low Free T4, and reports forgetting levothyroxine. Symptoms of tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes all point to inadequately treated hypothyroidism as the primary driver of weight gain. Evidence against DTG attribution: the guideline-cited association is non-causal. Evidence for non-drug cause: severe biochemical hypothyroidism from poor adherence fully explains the presentation.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise levothyroxine adherence and dose before considering DTG switch. Recheck TSH after 6–8 weeks of consistent dosing. Address adherence barriers.

alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism with inadequate levothyroxine dose
alerts.message: TSH 12.4 mIU/L with low Free T4 indicates current levothyroxine 50 mcg is insufficient. Patient admits often forgetting the thyroid tablet, explaining poor control. Symptoms include tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes — all classic hypothyroidism signs. The plan to simply continue levothyroxine 50 mcg without addressing adherence or dose escalation is inadequate. Untreated hypothyroidism also contributes to dyslipidaemia, compounding the elevated LDL and total cholesterol.

evidence.recommended_action: Increase levothyroxine dose and implement adherence support. Recheck TSH and Free T4 after 6–8 weeks. Counsel on importance of daily dosing.

alerts.title: Elevated lipids and fasting glucose — metabolic risk assessment needed
alerts.message: Guidelines identify BMI ≥25 and age ≥30 as hyperglycaemia risk factors requiring glucose monitoring in patients on DTG. This patient meets both criteria (BMI 33, age 45). Fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L is borderline. LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4, and triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L are all elevated. Undertreated hypothyroidism is a significant contributor to dyslipidaemia. The clinician's plan does not address lipid abnormalities or arrange follow-up metabolic monitoring. Weight gain plus dyslipidaemia plus borderline glucose creates compounding cardiovascular risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Address hypothyroidism control first, then reassess lipid panel. Consider dietary intervention and follow-up fasting glucose monitoring per DTG risk-factor guidelines.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue per DTG guideline schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines state patients on DTG-based first-line ART with VL <50 copies/mL for >1 year and reliable adherence can reduce VL monitoring to 12-monthly; otherwise check every 6 months. Last VL was <50 copies/mL on 2025-11-10, 106 days ago. If prior VL was also suppressed >1 year ago, a 12-month interval is acceptable. However, if the 1-year suppression milestone has not been met, a 6-month VL is due around May 2026. The clinician's plan does not mention any VL monitoring schedule.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm whether VL has been suppressed <50 for >1 year. If yes, next VL due Nov 2026. If not, schedule VL for May 2026 per 6-monthly monitoring.
